question: to the Commission Andrea Wechsler (PPE), Letizia Moratti (PPE), Marie-Sophie Lanig (PPE), Andreas Schwab (PPE), Alexandra Mehnert (PPE), Eva Maydell (PPE), Stefan Köhler (PPE), Markus Ferber (PPE), Christian Doleschal (PPE), Axel Voss (PPE), Angelika Winzig (PPE), Matej Tonin (PPE), Angelika Niebler (PPE), François-Xavier Bellamy (PPE), Ralf Seekatz (PPE), Verena Mertens (PPE), Susana Solís Pérez (PPE), Christian Ehler (PPE) Subject:

On 15 July 2026, the Commission opened infringement procedures against all 27 Member States for failing to fully transpose Directive (EU) 2024/1275 by 29 May 2026. The unprecedented fact that not a single Member State has completed transposition on time raises serious concerns about the practicability, proportionality and legal clarity of the directive. It also calls into question whether Member States were given sufficient time and sufficiently precise guidance, particularly as the Commission’s detailed support package was adopted only in June 2025 and important delegated and implementing acts followed thereafter. 1.

Will the Commission publish, for each Member State and provision, which transposition measures remain outstanding and identify the principal legal, technical and practical challenges to implementation, including insufficient building-stock data, administrative capacity, skilled labour, financing and legal uncertainty?

In view of the difficulties affecting all Member States, does the Commission envisage targeted amendments or a revision of the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive to address implementation challenges?
